next.reason: 1985: 'Violation of the rules for evaluation of exponentiation always terminates the arithmetic operation and always causes a size error condition.' 2023: the size error condition exists 'if the rules for evaluation of exponentiation are violated' (§2023:14.7.5 GR1), and §2023:8.8.1.2 GR6 says on each violation 'the EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION exception condition is set to exist and the size error condition is raised'. The operation is abandoned: with the SIZE ERROR phrase 'the values of all of the resultant data items remain unchanged' (§2023:14.7.5, catalog GR-14.7.5-L2.1), and 'If the size error condition is raised during the initial evaluation, none of the resultant data items are changed' (§2023:14.7.7 GR4). Both effects are kept. Which values violate the rules (VI.6.2.3) and what happens without the phrase (the fatal EC-SIZE handling replacing 1985's 'undefined' resultants) belong to other 1985 rules.
